9
In which situation is total linear momentum always conserved?
A
in all collisions between two objects
B
in collisions between two objects moving at equal and opposite velocity
C
in collisions between two objects that form an isolated system
D
in collisions between two objects with the same mass

hints: Focus on the word always in the stem and the phrase isolated system in one option, meaning no resultant external force acts on the two objects.
Recall that in a collision the two objects exert equal and opposite internal forces on each other by Newton's third law, so those impulses cancel for the total.
Ask whether equal velocity, equal mass, or simply having a collision removes external impulses like friction - only one condition guarantees $F_{ext} = 0$.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the condition that guarantees total linear momentum of the two colliding objects does not change.
State the governing rule: total momentum is conserved when the resultant external force is zero, because $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, so $\Delta p = 0$ when $F_{ext} = 0$.
Define an isolated system as two objects with only internal forces between them and no net external force or impulse from outside.

Check the other cases: any collision can have friction or a wall pushing from outside, equal and opposite velocities only set a particular initial momentum, and equal masses only affect $p = mv$ values.
Therefore only the isolated-system condition always gives conservation. This is option C.

A.explanation: Not all two-object collisions are isolated because an external force such as friction can act and change total momentum.

B.explanation: Equal and opposite velocity only makes the initial total momentum zero in a special case and does not remove external forces.

C.explanation: An isolated system has no resultant external force, so internal action-reaction forces cancel and total momentum $p = mv$ stays constant.

D.explanation: Equal masses do not guarantee zero external force, so total momentum can still be changed by friction or other external impulses.
